territorial_scope.description: Federal U.S. statute amending the Communications Act of 1934 for social media platforms within the United States.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled

summary.short: Amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 to remove liability protection for social media platforms that fail to use reasonable care in designing and operating recommendation-based algorithms causing bodily injury or death, and allows private damages suits. No commencement date is stated.
summary.long: The bill adds a new subsection (f) to Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 230) for providers of social media platforms. A provider must exercise reasonable care in the design, training, testing, deployment, operation and maintenance of a recommendation-based algorithm to prevent bodily injury or death that a reasonable and prudent person would agree was reasonably foreseeable and attributable in whole or in part to the algorithm's design characteristics or performance. Ranking by chronological order, or in response to an individual user search, is excepted, except after a user navigates beyond the initially populated search results. The duty may not be enforced by the Commission based on viewpoint protected by the First Amendment. A provider that violates the duty loses the protection of subsection (c)(1). A injured person, or a legal representative, may bring a civil action in federal district court for compensatory and punitive damages. Predispute arbitration agreements and joint-action waivers are invalid for disputes under the subsection, and courts decide their applicability. Federal and State laws at least as protective of users are not affected, and a severability clause applies. For-profit interactive computer services are covered if they meet a profile test, and services with fewer than 1,000,000 registered users, email, direct messaging, internal enterprise, certain video conferencing, and certain review, commerce, music and news platforms are excluded. Conforming amendments replace references to Section 230(f) in the Trademark Act of 1946, title 18 section 2421A, the Webb-Kenyon Act and title 31 section 5362(6). The text states no commencement date.

relations.note: Adds new subsection (f), Algorithmic product design accountability, and redesignates former subsection (f) as subsection (g).
